title.rendered: You Are the Light of the World: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father.” A morning devotional on the borrowed brightness of a follower of Christ.

content.rendered:
An astronaut looking down at earth at night sees the world in a completely different way. The continents disappear. What remains, glowing against the darkness, are the cities. Every city, every town, every village, contributing to the light. Jesus said the believer, in the darkness of the world, is meant to shine like that.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, September 6, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden. Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a basket, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.”
Matthew 5:14-16 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

An astronaut looking down at earth from the International Space Station sees the world in a way no one on the ground ever will. During the day, the continents dominate the view. At night, the continents disappear. What remains, glowing against the darkness, are the cities. Every city, every town, every village, every home, contributing to the light. Lagos glows on the West African coast. Manila glows in the Philippines. London glows on the Thames. Nairobi glows in the Rift Valley. From space, the human presence on earth is measured in light. Jesus said the believer, in the darkness of the world, is meant to shine like that.

“You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden.” Jesus is continuing the Sermon on the Mount. Having called His disciples the salt of the earth, He now calls them the light of the world. Two identity statements. Both delivered as present-tense fact. You are. Not you might become. Not you should try. You are.

Notice the shift from an earlier “I am” statement. In John 8, Jesus said, “I am the light of the world.” Here in Matthew 5, He says to His disciples, “You are the light of the world.” The two statements are not in conflict. They are in relationship. Jesus is the source. The disciples are the reflection. Just as the moon has no light of its own but reflects the light of the sun, the believer has no light of their own but reflects the light of Christ. When the world sees the good works of the disciple, they are not admiring the disciple. They are being drawn to the Father the disciple points to.

The Passion Translation opens up the calling: “Your lives light up the world. Let others see your light from a distance, for how can you hide a city that stands on a hilltop? And who would light a lamp and then hide it in an obscure place? Instead, it’s placed where everyone in the house can benefit from its light. So don’t hide your light! Let it shine brightly before others, so that the commendable things you do will shine as light upon them, and then they will give their praise to your Father in heaven” (Matthew 5:14-16 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden” (Matthew 5:14 AMPC). Cannot be hidden. The light of a Christ-formed life is meant to be seen.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is your identity in a watching world. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, you are the light of the world. Not a light. The light. You do not need to manufacture the light. Christ has already lit it in you by His Spirit. Your part is not to hide it, not to dim it out of false humility, not to let the darkness intimidate you into a smaller glow. Let your light shine. Let your good works be seen. And when others notice the difference, do not point them back to yourself. Point them to the Father in heaven, who is the Source of every light that has ever lit up any life. Today closes ten days of walking through the opening of the Sermon on the Mount, from the poor in spirit to the light of the world. The whole arc has one destination. A Kingdom people, formed by grace, shining together as one collective light in a watching world.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have made me the light of the world in Christ. This is not my light. It is Yours, lit in me by the Spirit of Your Son. Today I refuse to hide it. I refuse to dim it out of false humility. I refuse to let the darkness intimidate me into a smaller glow. I let my light shine. I let my good works be seen. And when others notice the difference, I point them back to You, the Source of every light that has ever lit up any life. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am the light of the world in Christ. My light is His light, lit in me by the Spirit. I refuse to hide it. I let it shine. My good works point to the Father, not to me.
